takeoff_timeline.root_cause: IMPLEMENTER HARNESS DEFECT (attempt-3 author), rails behaved as designed: run_speech_native_agent_loop derives ORG/SUPPLY/USE trace record ids from sample_id + '/agent-loop/...' with NO arm or micro-run discriminator, and TraceSink.emit refuses duplicate ids by design. The canary micro-run flushed agent-loop records for samples 000090 and 000109 into the attempt's single shared trace sink; the BLEND loop over the full split regenerated those ids for the same two samples, so the BLEND buffer's flush collided on its first 000090 record and raised, discarding the un-emitted remainder of the buffer. The SAME latent collision exists in the attempt-2 launcher's never-reached resend flush (resend re-runs sample 000090 through the loop after BLEND's flush): attempt 2 would have hit it at the resend. The attempt-3 canary moved the collision AHEAD of the BLEND flush, which upgraded the would-be loss (resend record only) into the full BLEND response loss. Correct fix for any future attempt: flush every micro-run (canary, resend) into its OWN trace file via a dedicated sink, never into the shared client sink; and flush the main arm FIRST.
